Understanding Rates
About Electricity Delivery
In Alberta, distribution companies (like ATCO) and retailers work together to bring you electricity. We, your electricity distribution company, deliver electricity to you. Your retailer sells you your electricity, provides account services and bills you. You're free to purchase electricity services from a retailer of your choice. You can get more information about retailers through the
Utility Consumer Advocate
.
You rely on your electricity being there to light your home, charge your phone, cook your dinner, wash your clothes, and keep your porch light on. We've been energizing homes, farms, and businesses for more than 85 years.
We deliver electricity to nearly 229,000 customers in north and east-central Alberta.
How to Read Your Bill
Electricity. You use it daily. But chances are, you don’t think much about it until it’s time to pay the bill. So, what do those charges really mean? What does electricity actually cost? And what value are you getting?
How to Read Your Bill
How Rates are Determined
We work around the clock to make sure the power is there when your home, farm or business needs it. The approved distribution tariffs we collect let us continue providing this service safely and reliably. Your cost for electricity delivery includes distribution tariffs and rate riders.

Choose a fixed or floating electricity rate for 1, 2, 3 or 5 years. You’re free to change plans at any time.
Fixed electricity rate
For every kWh of electricity you use, the fixed price is an all-in rate that your consumption will be based on. Because your consumption will vary from month to month, your energy charge will vary, but the unit price won’t!
A fixed electricity price is a stable rate option that gives you predictability for the term of your plan. When the market fluctuates, your price per kWh remains constant.
The fixed price is ideal for customers wishing to minimize volatility in their energy charges from month to month.
Floating electricity rate
The price of electricity on the market fluctuates every hour and appears on your bill as a weighted monthly average. With our Floating Rate Plan, your rate follows the market and can fluctuate up and down based on several factors like supply, demand, and the weather.
The floating electricity rate is suitable for customers who are comfortable with some variability in their rates in exchange for potential savings when market prices are low.
Not sure what to choose? We can help.
We'll walk you through the options to build your perfect plan.
Contact Customer Care
Choose a fixed or floating natural gas rate for 1, 2, 3 or 5 years.
Fixed natural gas rate
A fixed natural gas rate won’t fluctuate when the market changes. It’s a stable rate option that gives you predictability for the term of your plan. When the market fluctuates, your price per GJ remains constant.
For every GJ of natural gas you use, the Fixed Price is an all-in rate that your consumption will be charged on. Because the amount of natural gas you use will vary from month-to-month, your energy charge will vary, but the unit price won’t.
The fixed rate is ideal for customers who might not mind paying a bit more in exchange for stability in their energy every month.
Floating natural gas rate
Natural gas prices fluctuate every month as the actual market price changes.
With our Floating Rate Plan, what you pay for natural gas (per GJ) will rise or fall each month based on market activity. Your natural gas rate is based on a temperature-weighted average flow-through of the market price, which tends to rise during colder months when demand for heating increases.
The floating natural gas rate is suitable for customers who are willing to experience monthly ups and downs in their energy bills in exchange for potential savings over time.
Not sure what to choose? We can help.
We'll walk you through the options to build your perfect plan.

You can choose to supplement your electricity plan by making it green.
‍
Green energy comes from renewable sources like hydro, wind, and solar. The creation of electricity through these sources creates a Renewable Energy Certificate (REC), which is a means of controlling the finite inventory of electrons that were generated.
‍
As a consumer, you can select from 25% or 100% of your electri
[DOC 1] https://energy.atco.com/home-energy
city plan from ATCO Energy to come from renewable sources for a small premium. The green premium is charged on your consumption in kWh.
‍
Based on your selected green percentage, your consumption is calculated to ensure you’ve been allocated the right amount of green energy and that the RECs are retired on your behalf.
Not sure what to choose? We can help.
We'll walk you through the options to build your perfect plan.

Floating rates
Nobody knows the ups and downs of a market like you, a business owner. Our floating rates depend on the actual market price. If the market rates for electricity or natural gas fluctuates, so do yours.
‍
Instead of paying for a stable rate under the fixed rate model, your charges are based on flow-through of the market price for the electricity and natural gas provided to you, plus a minimal service fee. This means you could save one month but spend a bit more the next as the market fluctuates.
Our floating rate plans provide exposure to the market and are suited to businesses that are willing to experience volatility in their energy charges, as both their consumption and the rate will vary every month.

Feb 26, 2024
Alberta electricity rates & prices
Find out how electricity rates are determined in Alberta and the difference between a competitive retailer and the Rate of Last Resort.
Home and business owners in Alberta often have questions about their electricity bills. How are electricity prices set? Who sets electricity prices? How can you find the best electricity prices for your home or business?
You’ll find everything you need to know about how electricity rates and prices are determined in Alberta below.
How are energy rates in Alberta determined?
Electricity is measured by kilowatt per hour (kWh) and you’re charged a kWh price that’s multiplied by the amount of electricity you use.
As a guideline, one kWh is the amount of energy that 1,000 watts consume in an hour. For example, a 100-watt light bulb uses one kWh every 10 hours. If you’re paying 4c/kWh, that light bulb is costing you 4 cents for every 10 hours that it’s on.
On average, a home in Alberta uses 7,200 kWh of electricity a year, although monthly usage can vary with the season. However, two households with the same level of consumption can still have vastly different bills.
How can that be?
Regulated rates vs competitive retail rates
Households and businesses in Alberta have had access to retailer-provided electricity since 2001 when the process of deregulation, which began in 1996, started gaining steam.
Now, there are essentially two ways to be billed for the electricity you use in Alberta:
1. Regulated rates
Electricity is traded as a commodity. By default, Albertans can choose between regulated retailer rates set by the
Alberta Utilities Commission (AUC)
or a competitive retailer like ATCO Energy.
The Rate of Last Resort (RoLR)
is primarily designed as a safety net for those who don’t qualify for a competitive option. If someone can't meet the credit requirements to enroll or remain with a supplier, the RoLR ensures they still receive a power supply.
The AUC approves regulated rates, which vary by service area. RoLR customers are subject to all pricing fluctuations influenced by market conditions, the current economy and more.
In 2017, a Regulated Rate Cap of 6.8 ¢/kWh was introduced, but it was removed in 2019. The cost to subsidize the cap was enormous. Even though competitive options were available well below the capped rate were readily available, subsidizing the rate cap cost Albertans nearly $100 million to discount the rate.
Learn more about the Rate of Last Resort
.
2. Competitive retail rates
These are based on the current prices offered by retail energy providers and give you more flexibility in
choosing an energy plan
.
Most retailers give you the option to choose between paying a fixed rate or a floating rate with a built-in retail markup price added.
Why is the Rate of Last Resort less than ideal?
Since the Rate of Last Resort is the default option, it gives you less control over your plan. The RoLR doesn’t come with the perks, flexibility, or rate choices of a 
[DOC 6] https://energy.atco.com/en-ca/blog/alberta-electricity-rates-prices.html
retail plan.
While the RoLR offers a fixed rate over a two-year term, it doesn't necessarily guarantee stable prices during the term. Changes in market conditions can cause the rate to increase even during the two-year period, making it less predictable than it might seem at first glance.
Take control of your bill. There's no time to wait.
Switch today
.
Competitive retail rates
With competitive retail rate options, you have the freedom and ability to shop around in a deregulated market. Some of the choices offered by competitive retailers are extremely attractive.
You can choose an electricity provider and plan that works specifically for your own energy use in your home or business.
At ATCO Energy, we offer energy plans tailored to homes and businesses. These plans come with lots of choice and flexibility, and you're free to switch, cancel or change plans anytime.
For homeowners,
fixed and floating electricity rates
give you freedom and control over your electricity plan choices.
Businesses can choose between
fixed and floating rates
, and have access to
local business energy experts.
1. Fixed rate
A fixed rate is a stable rate option that gives you predictability for the term of your plan. When the market fluctuates, your price per kilowatt hour (kWh) remains constant.
You'll pay a guaranteed all-in rate based on your consumption for every kWh of electricity you use. Because your consumption will vary from month to month, your energy charge will vary, but the price you pay for each kWh won’t.
The fixed rate is ideal for customers looking to minimize volatility in their energy charges from month to month.
2. Floating rate
A floating rate provides more flexibility because it doesn't lock you into a fixed price.
The price of electricity on the market fluctuates throughout the day and appears on your bill as a weighted monthly average. The floating rate option follows these market prices, and a retail markup is added on to every kWh consumed.
Floating rates can change due to weather, demand spikes, or disruptions in power generation. This option suits customers who are comfortable with market unpredictability and willing to take risks.
What is the difference between competitive retailers and the Rate of Last Resort (RoLR)?
As you already know, competitive retailers offer deregulated rate options including a floating rate and a fixed rate, while the RoLR is a regulated option.
Fixed rates vs. floating rates
Think of interest rates for mortgages when buying a house.
Some people prefer the safety of knowing how much their payments will be each month for years ahead while others prefer to pay a flexible, floating rate based on market conditions.
Those who prefer a floating rate will select from a range of options offered by a broker or directly with the bank. Many of these same mortgage providers will also offer a fixed rate option.
Buying a home is such a major investment that even minor fluctuations in interest rates can impact the monthly layout on
[DOC 6] https://energy.atco.com/en-ca/blog/alberta-electricity-rates-prices.html
 the mortgage – thousands and thousands of dollars over the course of a few years.
As a general rule, when the interest rates start to fall, floating rates are more attractive and when they start to rise, fixed rates become more attractive.
Just like your fixed rate mortgage, fixed rates stay the same no matter how high or how low market rates go.
Floating rates, on the other hand, follow market prices along with built-in markup for every bit of electricity used.
When assessing which is best for your home, it helps to analyze not only current energy rates but also the historical averages and electricity rate trends in Alberta.
What are the other costs besides electricity (kWh) usage on your bill?
To receive electricity to your premises, you need a distributor and a retailer.
Both technically and legally, these companies must be separated. Even though the same parent company can provide both (e.g., ATCO Energy and ATCO Gas), there is a “firewall” between regulated and deregulated services. This is to protect the customer by making sure all distributors treat Albertans equally, no matter who they choose as their retailer.
However, you will receive one bill from the retailer that also includes fees and charges from your distributor.
While your electricity usage and rate factor into your bill, they aren't the biggest component. Retailers primarily earn from your usage costs. However, other charges go to the companies that generate and deliver energy to your home.
The usage costs largely compensate the retailer, but other charges are flow-through charges remitted to the companies that generate and deliver the energy to your home.
These charges mainly cover the installation, operation, and maintenance of the infrastructure used to transmit and deliver energy to your home.
So, other charges apart from the actual electricity usage appearing on your bill may include:
Transmission charges (quarterly transmission riders that may be credits or charges)
Distribution/delivery charges
Local access fees
Balancing pool riders
Transmission access rider
Various other charges, such as a
Rural Electrification Association (REA)
charge, may appear on your bill if you're on the Rate of Last Resort option.
Understanding distribution and transmission charges
You already know that the more electricity you use, the higher your bill. But the AUC
estimates
that only 19-35 percent of the average bill is energy usage.
As well as the cost of usage, your bill comprises the additional components detailed above. The major items involve the costs of generating and transporting electricity across the province.
So, the
distribution charge
will make up between 24 and 52 percent of the total average bill and the
transmission charge
will comprise 13-23 percent of the total.
Distribution charges cover the costs incurred by the distribution company that delivers electricity from the transmission system to your home using poles, wires, etc.
Costs cover three main elements of the distributio
[DOC 6] https://energy.atco.com/en-ca/blog/alberta-electricity-rates-prices.html
n system:
Building the system
Operating the system
Maintaining the system
Your bill includes a fixed fee, based on the number of days in the billing period, plus a variable component that is based on your energy usage.
Think of the fixed component as the “price of entry” that everybody pays to the grid. If you receive electricity from it and your power flows through it, whether you use it or not, you need to pay it.
So, if you go on holiday and only use a tiny amount of electricity in a particular month, you’ll still have a distribution charge included on your monthly bill. Because you used less electricity for the billing period, though, the variable charges would be lower.
The transmission charge covers the costs of planning Alberta’s transmission grid and transporting electricity via the grid from where it is generated to the distribution system.
These charges vary according to usage for homeowners and, for businesses in Alberta, the transmission charge becomes a little more complex.
Note that your payments include maintenance and upgrades of the grid. The transmission component of your bill may increase as this helps to protect the continuous and efficient supply of electricity to your premises wherever you are in Alberta.
Learn more about the charges included in your energy bills
.
How can you compare electricity rates in Alberta?
The Utilities Consumer Advocate website is a good resource for Albertans who want to find out more about the electricity rates, and it includes a
cost comparison tool
. The website
www.energyrates.ca
also provides a comprehensive comparison tool. You’ll notice that retail rates are highly competitive, and rates often differ by only a fraction of a cent. So you’ll also want to consider things like administration fees, customer service and whether or not it’s a local company investing in Alberta’s communities.
What are your options with ATCO Energy?
ATCO Energy provides fixed rate and floating rate plans for electricity customers.
The
fixed rate
is provided via plans that range from one to three years in length. You’re typically rewarded with a lower rate for signing up for the longer plans, even though you’re not locked in and can change your mind any time.
A fixed rate helps you predict your bills over the next 12, 24, or 36 months due to the stable rate offered.
The
floating rate
is a market rate plan that provides more flexibility.
There may be spikes over time, especially during the winter. However, with this option, when rates are low, your bill will be lower and during the course of the year, floating rates tend to be the better value.
Bear in mind that whether you opt for a fixed rate or a floating, you're never locked in to your plan. It’s flexible and you are not bound by long-term commitments so you can switch anytime.
Our rates and term lengths are our guarantees to you, but you're free to change your plan anytime.

What you need to know about the
Rate of Last Resort
(RoLR)
We’ve laid out all the info you need to understand Alberta’s changes to electricity rates.
What is the Rate of Last Resort?
In January 2025, the Rate of Last Resort became the new default electricity rate in Alberta, replacing the
Regulated Rate Option (RRO)
. Unlike the RRO which adjusted monthly, the Rate ofLast Resort is a fixed rate for a two-year period with a potential increase of up to 10% after that term.
Starting in January 2027, a new RoLR term begins
The current Rate of Last Resort term ends on December 31, 2026. Beginning January 1, 2027, a new rate will take effect for the next two-year period. The RoLR is reviewed every two years and may change for the next term. This plan automatically applies to anyone who hasn’t chosen a competitive retailer for their home or business energy needs.
Looking for more certainty?
While the Rate of Last Resort is the default option for electricity in Alberta, itʼs not the mostaffordable.
Exploring more affordable and flexible plans with competitive retailers like
ATCO Energy
could offer the stability and peace of mind you need. Our fixed rates are guaranteed because they will not change for the duration of your term.

FrequentLY ASKED questions
Rate of Last Resort FAQs
What’s the reason for the RRO name change?
The Government of Alberta believes changing the name of the Regulated Rate Option (RRO) to the Rate of Last Resort (RoLR) better reflects its true nature. The term ‘regulated’ might have lead some to mistakenly believe it was immune to market fluctuations.
By renaming it, the government aims to make it clear that this is a default option, prompting Albertans to explore their other options, like
fixed rate plans
, which could offer more stability and potential savings.
Do I need to switch from the RRO/Rate of Last Resort?
There’s no requirement to switch but doing so may save you money and provide more flexibility in managing your energy expenses.
Are natural gas rates affected by this change?
No, the Rate of Last Resort only impacts electricity rates. But choosing a
competitive retailer for your natural gas
offers similar saving opportunities.
How can I prepare for the transition?
You have the power to choose a better option. Start by exploring competitive energy plans that offer lower rates and more flexibility than the Rate of Last Resort.
We provide a
range of options
that can be tailored to your needs, allowing you to make an informed choice.

The quarterly $50 rebate program requires an active account and good financial standing for 90 days prior, with rebates being applied when a service is completed and expiring at the end of each quarter. Rebates cannot be combined with other quarterly rebates or carried forward to subsequent periods. Furnace Family Maintenance Plans subscriptions are not eligible to be covered by your quarterly rebate and are billed separately. This program may be modified or discontinued at our discretion.
